MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 24, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:01 p.m., on September 24, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 19, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiator, Government Code Section 54956.8. The
  Property Commonly Referred to as "Casta del Sol Golf Course" located at 27601
  Casta del Sol, Mission Viejo, California. City of Mission Viejo Negotiators: City
  manager Dennis Wilbert, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith
  Rattay, Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas and City Attorney William
  Curley, III. Negotiating Party: American Golf Corporation Mr. J. Hinckley,
  President and Mr. Foley, General Counsel Under Discussion Price and Terms.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project
  v. The City of Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  1  September 24, 2019
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed two topics in Closed Session. For
item CS1, the Council received an update on some changes in the details regarding the Casta del
Sol Golf Course which are reflected in open session agenda item #9. For item CS2, the Council
received updates and gave direction to staff but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Featured Businesses of the Month - Linda Rippin Estate Planning & Reverse Mortgage
  Advisor and Adagio on the Green

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamations to Linda Rippin and Lyn Eisert from Adagio on
  the Green.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Michael Rotcher, MV: Advocated for Community Choice Energy mainly on the basis of economic
opportunities and advantages. He spoke about fossil fuels and commented on the Climate Strike
that was held last week by students around the world. Mr. Rotcher urged the Council to look into
climate change issues.

Ingmar Forster, MV: Stated that he is not in favor of a hotel being built on City property near
Saddleback College. He suggested that the land be used for low income housing since the State is
mandating that more affordable housing be built.

Steven Brerezin, MV: Announced that there are still positions available for census takers and
supervisors for the 2020 Census. Those interested can go to the website, www.2020census.gov/
jobs or call (855) JOB-2020.

Ryan Farsai, MV: Spoke on various topics including his ongoing dispute with the electronic sign
behind the Arco station on the corner of Marguerite Parkway and La Paz Road.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  2  September 24, 2019
 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of September 10, 2019, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated August 30, 2019 in the Amount of $982,520.39

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated September 6, 2019 in the Amount of $743,841.66

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Marguerite Parkway Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP 17230)

  Authorized issuance of a purchase order to Iteris, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $65,000
  for design engineering services for Phase II (Operations & Maintenance) of Capital
  Improvement Project 17230.

5.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  (1) Adopted Resolution 19-30 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies; and
  (2) adopted Resolution 19-31 Establishing an Amended Employer-Employee Relations
  Resolution and Repealing Resolution 17-40.

6.  Safety Lighting LED Conversions (CIP 16228)

  (1) Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $94,178 to Express Energy Services,
  Inc., for safety lighting LED conversions; and (2) adopted Resolution 19-32 Amending the
  Fiscal Year 2019/2020 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Project 16228.

7.  Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Project (TRAP): Olympiad Road
  Bioretention Basins with Trash Capture (CIP 20245)

  Adopted Resolution 19-33 Amending the Fiscal Year 2019/2020 Budget to Create Capital
  Improvement Program Project 20245 for the Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement
  Project (TRAP): Olympiad Road Bioretention Basins with Trash Capture.

8.  Contract for the Operation of the MV Shuttle

  (1) Awarded the Contract to LAZ Parking California, LLC., in the amount of $300,000 for
  the operation of the MV Shuttle; and (2) adopted Resolution 19-36 Amending the Fiscal
  Year 2019/2020 Budget for Costs Related to the Operation of the MV Shuttle (Program 225).

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
City Council Minutes  3  September 24, 2019
 OLD BUSINESS

9.  Purchase of Casta Del Sol Public Golf Property for the Purpose of Preserving the Golf
  Course and Open Space

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Written comments were received from resident Cathy Schlicht voicing opposition to the
  purchase of the Casta del Sol Golf Course. She also expressed concerns with some of the
  costs outlined in the staff report and the 20-year projection for the golf course.

  Bob Breton, MV: Asked that the Council consider the purchase of the golf course for future
  generations and stated it will be a great asset to the City.

  Ingmar Forster, MV: Spoke against the purchase of the golf course. He expressed that the
  taxpayers don’t need to buy the land in order to control the land. He also said he is in favor
  of the golf course remaining a golf course or open space.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to continue
  the item to the October 8, 2019, meeting for continued public input and to vote on the
  purchase of the golf course.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

10. Parking Restrictions on Public Streets

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to
  Introduce Ordinance 19-331 Amending Chapter 12.08.010 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code Regarding Parking Restrictions on Public Streets.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11. Fiscal Year 2018/19 Close Out Report and Fiscal Year 2019/20 Budget Adjustments for
  Certain Revenue and Expenditure Accounts

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  4  September 24, 2019
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 19-34 Amending the FY 2018/19 City Budget for Year-End Close Out
  Adjustments in Certain Accounts and Funds; and (2) adopt Resolution 19-35 Amending the
  FY 2019/20 City Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

12. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum stated that she attended the Buy Local Showcase at the Village
Shopping Center and she gave kudos to the Chamber of Commerce for the successful event. She
suggested that perhaps the program could be spread throughout the City at other centers in the
future. She also outlined her attendance at the Patriot Day event at the Murray community center
and said that the turnout was great and she thanked staff for their efforts. Council Member
Bucknum spoke about the MV Shuttle agenda item that was on the Consent Calendar this evening
and pointed out that the City is taking over the service and will receive grant funding to cover 90%
of the cost. She highlighted three significant improvements: (1) an increase in vehicle capacity, (2)
automated passenger counters, and (3) a GPS smartphone app, that will allow City Staff and riders
to track vehicle locations and determine the approximate arrival times. Council Member Bucknum
asked the City Attorney to address the potential for a hotel near Saddleback College.

City Attorney Bill Curley responded that there is no official proposal and that it was only a
suggestion.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she attended and participated in the Intercoastal Cleanup
Day along Oso Creek trail with two of her grandchildren. She thanked Denise Matson and Joe
Ames for their work with the program. She also announced that there will be a Youth Drug Abuse
Prevention Expo on Wednesday, October 16, 2019, from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. at the Norman P.
Community Center. She stated that the event is free and there will be three guest speakers - an
emergency room doctor, a Community Resource Officer and a representative from Orange County
Health Care Agency. Council Member Kelley encouraged high school age students, parents and
teachers to attend and said that participants can registration on eventbright.com and search for the
event title, “Is it Worth it?”

City Council Minutes  5  September 24, 2019
 Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs complimented Council Member Kelley on her involvement in the Youth
Drug Abuse Prevention Expo and said he hopes that he will be able to attend. He wished Lieutenant
Vuong a happy belated birthday and he announced that on October 7, Secure OC Schools will be
conducting a parent demonstration in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. It will include a
demonstration of the phone app that is currently being created along with active shooter training.
Council Member Sachs encouraged parents to attend and he noted that they are looking into having
an evening demonstration in the future. Lastly, he asked the Mayor to close the meeting in memory
of Investment Advisory Commissioner Bill Ernisse who passed away recently.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell expressed his enthusiasm for the City’s potential acquisition of the Casta
del Sol Golf Course. He announced that the Olympic Promotion Committee will be meeting
tomorrow at 11:00 a.m. and will revisit the idea of a visitor bureau website to globally promote
events and venues within the City.

Mayor Raths

13. Purchase and Installation of the Stranded Heart Sculpture

  Mayor Raths presented his Council report.

  Kyle Brownfield, MV: Complimented the Council and the City Commissions on the great
  work they do. She stated that she is the Vice President of the Friends of the Arts and she
  gave an overview of the various events that the Friends are involved in. She expressed that
  she is very much in favor of the purchase of the Stranded Heart Sculpture.

  Motion made by Mayor Raths, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
  installation of the Stranded Heart Sculpture along the Lakeside Promenade on Alicia
  Parkway and amended the budget to include $17,500 for the purchase of the sculpture.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Raths thanked the Chamber of Commerce for an amazing Restaurant Week and Buy Local
Program.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:56 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting in memory of Investment Advisory Commissioner Bill
Ernisse, to Tuesday, October 8, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  6  September 24, 2019
 ______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 8, 2019

City Council Minutes  7  September 24, 2019
